correctness.rationale: For all \(q>1\), \(U>0\), \(t>0\) and \(b>0\), fixing \(U\) determines \(b=U\coth(t)-1\) on an explicit interval. The remaining \(G_U(t)\) has derivative \(2q^4\tanh(qt)[(1+q^4b)/(q^3\sinh(2qt))-(1+b)/\sinh(2t)]<0\) because \(\sinh(2qt)>q\sinh(2t)\) and \(1+q^4b<q^4(1+b)\). Sharp endpoint limits are \(L_q(U)\) and \(q^5U\), both excluded for finite positive depth and rigidity; continuity proves existence and global uniqueness exactly on that strict interval. The Jacobian has the claimed sign. Standalone numerical checker corroborates 120 cases but is not relied upon for infinite quantification. Applicable only to the explicitly stated ideal massless sheet.

value.rationale: Depth and bending rigidity enter the physical finite-depth hydroelastic dispersion through distinct nonlinear functions, so identifying them from the minimum two frequency observations is a natural inverse problem. The result classifies the entire feasible noise-free measurement cone for every wavelength ratio, rules out ambiguity globally, supplies a one-dimensional monotone reconstruction and identifies the exceptional ill-conditioning regimes. This is more useful than merely fitting two parameters numerically or recalculating the known forward dispersion.
